taxonomy.subtopic: Dual AV nodal pathways and initiation by a premature atrial impulse

questions.stem_html: A 28-year-old woman has sudden-onset palpitations. Electrocardiography shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 190/min with no clearly visible P waves. The rhythm terminates after intravenous adenosine. The accompanying diagram shows two functionally distinct pathways near the atrioventricular node. Which sequence most likely initiated the tachycardia?

options.text_html: A premature atrial impulse encountered a refractory fast pathway, traveled antegrade through the slow pathway, and returned retrograde through the recovered fast pathway
A sinus impulse traveled antegrade through both pathways simultaneously and entered the His bundle twice
A ventricular premature beat traveled retrograde through an accessory atrioventricular pathway and returned through ventricular myocardium
An atrial ectopic focus repeatedly discharged faster than the sinus node without participation of the AV node
Progressive slowing within the His-Purkinje system generated a ventricular reentry circuit

questions.explanation_html: Typical AV nodal reentrant tachycardia uses dual nodal physiology. The fast pathway conducts rapidly but has a longer refractory period; the slow pathway conducts slowly but recovers sooner. A premature atrial beat may find the fast pathway refractory and descend through the slow pathway. The delay permits fast-pathway recovery, retrograde conduction, and a self-sustaining slow-fast circuit. Adenosine transiently blocks AV nodal conduction and interrupts the loop.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Simultaneous antegrade conduction does not establish the required unidirectional block and reentrant loop.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: This is closer to atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia using an accessory pathway.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: A focal atrial tachycardia is driven by automaticity or triggered activity and may continue despite transient AV block.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: A ventricular circuit generally produces a wide-complex tachycardia and is not expected to terminate through transient AV nodal block.

questions.educational_objective: Typical AVNRT begins when a premature atrial impulse is blocked in a refractory fast pathway, conducts antegrade through a slow pathway, and returns retrograde through the recovered fast pathway.
